q: After a notice inviting tenders for a work has been issued, a material change in the tender conditions or in the scope of the work becomes necessary before the due date of submission. Such a change is properly brought to the notice of all prospective tenderers by:

options.A: An oral intimation given to the tenderers who happen to visit the office
options.B: A note recorded only in the office file, the tenders being opened as scheduled
options.C: Altering the copies of the tender document already sold, without any public notice
options.D: Issuing a corrigendum to the tender notice, allowing such further time for submission as the change may reasonably require

e: A material change in tender conditions or scope after issue of the notice is properly notified to all prospective tenderers by a corrigendum to the tender notice, allowing further time for submission as reasonably required.

q: The principal purpose of holding a pre-bid conference in connection with a major or complex tender is to:

options.A: Clarify the tenderers' doubts about the tender documents, site conditions and scope of work before they submit their bids, the clarifications being issued to all concerned
options.B: Negotiate the rates quoted by the lowest tenderer
options.C: Open the financial bids of the tenderers in their presence
options.D: Distribute the work among the tenderers present at the conference

e: A pre-bid conference is held to clarify tenderers' doubts about the tender documents, site conditions and scope before bids are submitted, the clarifications being issued to all concerned.

q: 'Two-stage bidding' is adopted for a complex work or procurement mainly because:

options.A: It enables the work to be split into two contracts of equal value
options.B: It fixes two separate completion dates for the same work
options.C: In the first stage the technical proposals are discussed and finalised without prices, and price bids are invited in the second stage only for the firmed-up specification, so that bids are comparable
options.D: It dispenses with the security deposit in the second stage of the work

e: In two-stage bidding, technical proposals are first discussed and finalised without prices, and price bids are invited in the second stage only for the firmed-up specification, so bids are comparable.

q: Under the Quality-cum-Cost Based Selection method for engaging a consultant, the selection is made on the basis of:

options.A: The lowest fee quoted, the technical score being disregarded after eligibility
options.B: A combined score of the technical proposal and the financial proposal, weighted as notified in the request for proposals
options.C: The highest technical score alone, the fee being negotiated afterwards without limit
options.D: The recommendation of the consultant engaged for the previous assignment

e: Under Quality-cum-Cost Based Selection, the consultant is chosen on a combined score of the technical and financial proposals, weighted as notified in the request for proposals.

q: Under the Fixed Budget Selection method of engaging a consultant:

options.A: The consultant is selected solely on the basis of the lowest fee, whatever his technical merit
options.B: No budget is indicated to the competing consultants at any stage
options.C: The selection is made by nomination because the budget is fixed
options.D: The budget available for the assignment is indicated in advance, and the consultant who submits the best technical proposal within that budget is selected

e: Under Fixed Budget Selection, the budget is indicated in advance and the consultant submitting the best technical proposal within that budget is selected, not simply the lowest fee.

q: In the procurement of a large public-private partnership project, the Request for Qualification (RFQ) stage serves principally to:

options.A: Shortlist, on the basis of the applicants' technical and financial capacity, those who will be invited to submit detailed proposals for the project
options.B: Fix the concession fee payable by the selected concessionaire
options.C: Record the measurements of the work executed by the concessionaire
options.D: Replace the concession agreement for the project

e: The Request for Qualification stage of a PPP procurement shortlists applicants, on technical and financial capacity, who will be invited to submit detailed proposals for the project.

q: The 'Independent Engineer' appointed for a public-private partnership project of the Railways is engaged in order to:

options.A: Execute the project works departmentally on behalf of the concessionaire
options.B: Finance the project jointly with the concessionaire's lenders
options.C: Independently monitor the design, construction and operation of the project and certify matters assigned to him under the concession agreement
options.D: Audit the annual accounts of the Railway administration

e: The Independent Engineer in a PPP project independently monitors design, construction and operation of the project and certifies matters assigned to him under the concession agreement.

q: A 'substitution agreement' forming part of the documents of a public-private partnership project principally protects the project lenders by:

options.A: Guaranteeing a fixed return on the money lent by them in all circumstances
options.B: Giving them the right, on the concessionaire's default, to substitute another entity in place of the concessionaire so that the project can continue
options.C: Transferring the ownership of the railway land to the lenders
options.D: Exempting the project from the conditions of the concession agreement

e: A substitution agreement protects project lenders by giving them the right, on the concessionaire's default, to substitute another entity in the concessionaire's place so the project can continue.

q: In the Works Programme of a Railway, the 'throwforward' of sanctioned works represents:

options.A: The amount spent on the works during the preceding financial year
options.B: The savings surrendered on works completed during the year
options.C: The budget allotment made for the works for the current year
options.D: The total estimated cost of the sanctioned works still remaining to be spent in the future years, that is, the committed liability carried forward beyond the year under consideration

e: Throwforward of sanctioned works is the total estimated cost still remaining to be spent in future years, that is the committed liability carried forward beyond the year under consideration.

q: The 'anticipated cost' of a work under execution, which is compared with its sanctioned estimate to watch for an excess, means:

options.A: The expenditure already incurred on the work, plus the liabilities outstanding, plus the expenditure still expected to be incurred to complete it, as assessed at the time of the review
options.B: Only the expenditure booked on the work up to the end of the last financial year
options.C: The amount of the final bill submitted by the contractor
options.D: The original abstract estimate of the work, without any revision

e: Anticipated cost of a work is expenditure already incurred, plus outstanding liabilities, plus expenditure still expected to complete it, as assessed at review, and is compared with the sanctioned estimate.

q: Before a new railway line, or a work materially affecting the running of trains, is opened for the public carriage of passengers, the sanction principally required is that of:

options.A: The tender committee of the zonal railway
options.B: The contractor who executed the work
options.C: The Commissioner of Railway Safety, after inspection and satisfaction that the line or work can be opened without danger to the public
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Before a new line or work materially affecting train running is opened for public carriage of passengers, sanction of the Commissioner of Railway Safety, after inspection, is principally required.

q: In an 'item-rate contract' for a work, the contractor is paid:

options.A: A fixed lump sum for the whole work, irrespective of the quantities executed
options.B: A percentage above or below the schedule of rates, applied to the total cost
options.C: His actual cost of execution plus an agreed fee, without reference to quantities
options.D: For the quantities of each item actually executed and measured, at the rate quoted and accepted for that item in the schedule

e: In an item-rate contract, the contractor is paid for quantities of each item actually executed and measured, at the rate quoted and accepted for that item in the schedule.

q: In a 'percentage-rate contract', the tenderer competes by quoting:

options.A: A separate rate for every item of the schedule
options.B: A single percentage above, below or at the rates of the applicable schedule of rates, at which he agrees to execute all the items of the work
options.C: Only the total estimated cost of the work in round figures
options.D: The percentage of the contract value he requires as mobilisation advance

e: In a percentage-rate contract, the tenderer quotes a single percentage above, below or at the applicable schedule of rates, at which he agrees to execute all items of the work.

q: The distinguishing feature of a 'lump-sum contract' for a work is that:

options.A: The contractor agrees to execute the complete work, as shown in the drawings and specifications, for a fixed total sum, payment not being based on item-wise measurement of quantities in the ordinary course
options.B: The contractor is paid the measured quantities at open market rates
options.C: No drawings or specifications are prepared for the work at all
options.D: The sum is paid to the contractor in advance before the work is started

e: A lump-sum contract is distinguished by the contractor agreeing to execute the complete work as per drawings and specifications for a fixed total sum, payment not being based on item-wise measurement ordinarily.

q: A 'cost-plus contract', under which the contractor is paid his actual cost of execution together with an agreed percentage or fee, is generally resorted to only where:

options.A: The work is a small routine repair in a running section
options.B: Open tenders have already fixed firm rates for every item of the work
options.C: The scope and quantum of the work cannot be defined with sufficient precision in advance for firm rates to be quoted, as in certain emergency or exploratory works
options.D: The contractor insists on it in preference to an item-rate contract

e: A cost-plus contract is resorted to only where scope and quantum cannot be defined precisely enough in advance for firm rates, as in certain emergency or exploratory works.

q: Where the accepting authority, instead of accepting the lowest tender as offered, makes a counter-offer of a lower rate to the lowest tenderer, such a counter-offer in tender practice amounts to:

options.A: Acceptance of the tender on the Railway's own terms without the tenderer's consent
options.B: A negotiation with the lowest tenderer, to be conducted and recorded in accordance with the rules governing negotiations
options.C: Rejection of all the tenders received for the work
options.D: An amendment of the notice inviting tenders after its issue

e: A counter-offer of a lower rate to the lowest tenderer amounts to a negotiation with the lowest tenderer, to be conducted and recorded in accordance with the rules governing negotiations.

q: A tender in which the tenderer has quoted disproportionately high rates for the items to be executed in the early stages of the work and correspondingly low rates for the later items, the total remaining competitive, is described as:

options.A: A percentage-rate tender
options.B: A front-loaded (unbalanced) tender, since the Railway would pay out a disproportionate share of the contract value in the early stages
options.C: A lump-sum tender
options.D: A deposit-work tender

e: Quoting high rates for early items and low rates for later items, total remaining competitive, is a front-loaded or unbalanced tender, since the Railway pays a disproportionate share in the early stages.

q: A single work is proposed to be split into several smaller works so that each part falls within the powers of sanction, or the tender limits, of a lower authority. Such splitting is:

options.A: Not permissible, a requirement being arranged artificially in parts to avoid the sanction or the tender procedure prescribed for the whole
options.B: Permissible whenever the division maintains a separate list of the parts
options.C: Permissible provided the total cost remains within the budget allotment
options.D: Compulsory for all works extending over more than one section

e: Splitting a single work into smaller parts to bring each within a lower authority's sanction or tender limits is not permissible; a requirement cannot be artificially arranged in parts to avoid the prescribed procedure for the whole.

q: The briefing note placed before a Tender Committee, along with the comparative statement of the tenders received, is intended to:

options.A: Record the measurements of the work already executed
options.B: Show the savings available under the sanctioned estimate of the work
options.C: Replace the minutes of the Tender Committee after its meeting
options.D: Present the facts of the case — the estimated rates and their justification, the tenders received, the credentials of the tenderers and the reasonableness of the rates — so that the Committee can make its recommendation

e: The briefing note with the comparative statement presents the facts - estimated rates and justification, tenders received, tenderers' credentials and reasonableness of rates - so the Tender Committee can make its recommendation.

q: Before the tender documents for a major work are issued, they are placed for the vetting of the Finance branch principally so that:

options.A: The rates of the schedule of rates are replaced by the market rates of the day
options.B: The contractor for the work can be selected in advance of the tender
options.C: The eligibility conditions, evaluation criteria, contract conditions and financial implications contained in the documents are examined for correctness and consistency before tenderers act on them
options.D: The budget allotment for the work for the next year is fixed

e: Tender documents for a major work are vetted by Finance before issue so eligibility conditions, evaluation criteria, contract conditions and financial implications are examined for correctness and consistency.

q: Soon after the award of a major work, the contractor is required to submit a detailed programme of execution, ordinarily in the form of a bar chart or network, principally so that:

options.A: The sanctioned estimate of the work can be revised at that stage itself
options.B: The sequence and timing of the successive activities, and the resources to be deployed on them, are fixed in advance and the progress of the work can be monitored against them
options.C: The rates quoted by the contractor can be re-negotiated activity-wise
options.D: The security deposit can be worked out as a percentage of each activity

e: The contractor's detailed execution programme, as a bar chart or network, fixes the sequence and timing of activities and resources in advance, so progress can be monitored against it.

q: A 'Quality Assurance Plan' submitted by a contractor for a work sets out:

options.A: The system of checks, tests, inspections and records by which he will ensure that the materials used and the work executed conform to the specifications of the contract
options.B: The list of works he has executed for other employers in the past
options.C: The programme for payment of wages to the labour engaged on the work
options.D: The arrangement proposed by him for insuring the work against fire

e: A Quality Assurance Plan sets out the system of checks, tests, inspections and records by which the contractor will ensure materials and work conform to the contract specifications.

q: 'Third-party inspection' resorted to in connection with a work or a supply differs from the inspection by the Railway's own officials in that:

options.A: It is carried out after the expiry of the maintenance period of the work
options.B: It dispenses with all inspection by the consignee at the destination
options.C: It is only a paper scrutiny of the bills passed for the work
options.D: The inspection and testing are carried out by an independent agency, other than the executing or indenting officials and the contractor, engaged for that purpose

e: Third-party inspection differs in that inspection and testing are carried out by an independent agency, other than the executing or indenting officials and the contractor, engaged for that purpose.

q: Materials brought to the site of a work by the contractor are tested and a lot is rejected as not conforming to the specification. The correct treatment of the rejected lot is that:

options.A: It may be used in a less important portion of the work at a reduced rate
options.B: It is taken into the Materials-at-Site account of the work
options.C: It shall not be incorporated in the work and is to be removed from the site by the contractor; material so rejected but used is liable to be removed and replaced at his cost
options.D: It is auctioned by the Railway and the sale proceeds credited to the work

e: A rejected lot of material shall not be incorporated in the work and must be removed from site by the contractor; rejected material used is liable to be removed and replaced at his cost.

q: Where a mobilisation advance paid to a contractor is secured by a bank guarantee, the guarantee serves to:

options.A: Replace the performance guarantee required under the contract
options.B: Protect the Railway's advance, the guarantee amount being available for invocation if the contractor fails to adjust or repay the advance as stipulated
options.C: Guarantee the quality of the work for the whole of its maintenance period
options.D: Enable the contractor to avoid furnishing any security deposit for the work

e: A bank guarantee securing a mobilisation advance protects the Railway's advance, the guarantee amount being available for invocation if the contractor fails to adjust or repay the advance as stipulated.

q: A maintenance contract for equipment is described as 'comprehensive' when:

options.A: The cost of spare parts and consumables required for the maintenance, as well as the labour for it, is included in the contractor's scope and price
options.B: Only the labour for maintenance is provided by the contractor and all spares are bought separately by the Railway
options.C: The equipment is maintained departmentally and the contractor only supervises it
options.D: The contract covers the supply of new equipment in place of the old one

e: A comprehensive maintenance contract includes spare parts and consumables as well as labour in the contractor's scope and price, unlike a contract covering labour only.

q: In a services contract governed by a service level agreement, a shortfall in the level of service actually rendered in a month is ordinarily dealt with by:

options.A: Cancelling the security deposit of the contractor for that month alone
options.B: Paying the full contract charges, the shortfall being noted for the next tender
options.C: Extending the contract period by the number of days of the shortfall
options.D: Deducting from the payment for that period the amount prescribed in the agreement for the deficiency in service, besides recording the default for action under the contract

e: Under a service level agreement, shortfall in service in a month is dealt with by deducting from that period's payment the amount prescribed for the deficiency, besides recording the default for contract action.

q: At the project-formulation stage for a novel or complex proposal, an 'Expression of Interest' is invited from firms principally in order to:

options.A: Award the work to the firm expressing interest first
options.B: Fix the rates at which the work will later be executed
options.C: Gauge the response and capacity available in the market and to help frame the scope and conditions on which detailed proposals will later be invited
options.D: Collect earnest money from a large number of firms

e: An Expression of Interest at project formulation gauges market response and capacity and helps frame the scope and conditions on which detailed proposals will later be invited; it does not award the work.

q: Works such as the provision of an additional line on a congested section, automatic signalling and additional crossing stations, undertaken primarily to increase the number of trains that can be run on the section, are grouped as:

options.A: Deposit works executed for outside bodies
options.B: Line capacity enhancement works, their object being to augment the throughput of the section
options.C: Ordinary repairs chargeable to the open line working expenses
options.D: Works of the Stores department for building up inventory

e: Works like an additional line on a congested section, automatic signalling and additional crossing stations, meant to increase trains that can be run, are grouped as line capacity enhancement works.

q: The designs and drawings for a major bridge or a complex structure are subjected to 'proof checking' in order to:

options.A: Have the design independently verified by an agency or expert other than the one who prepared it, before the work is executed on those drawings
options.B: Obtain the budget allotment for the work from the Railway Board
options.C: Prepare the completion drawings of the structure after its execution
options.D: Decide the agency to which the construction contract should be awarded

e: Proof checking has the design of a major bridge or complex structure independently verified by an agency or expert other than its preparer, before execution on those drawings.

q: At the time of the final settlement of a works contract, the contractor is ordinarily required to furnish a 'no-claim certificate' to record that:

options.A: He has not executed any work outside the sanctioned estimate
options.B: The Railway has no liability outstanding towards his labour
options.C: The performance guarantee furnished by him may be forfeited
options.D: Except for the amounts of the final settlement itself, he has no further claim against the Railway in connection with the contract

e: A no-claim certificate at final settlement records that, except for the amounts of the final settlement itself, the contractor has no further claim against the Railway in connection with the contract.

q: Under the 'Swiss challenge' method sometimes adopted for a project proposal received from a private proponent:

options.A: The proposal is accepted straightaway because it originated with the proponent
options.B: The project is executed departmentally after studying the proposal
options.C: The proposal is publicised and counter-proposals are invited from others, the original proponent being given the opportunity to match the best counter-proposal
options.D: The proposal is referred to a tender committee of the zonal railway for negotiation

e: Under the Swiss challenge method, the proposal is publicised and counter-proposals invited, the original proponent being given the opportunity to match the best counter-proposal.

q: The payment arrangement in an EPC (turnkey) contract ordinarily differs from that in an item-rate contract in that, in the EPC contract:

options.A: Payment is made in advance for the whole project before the designs are prepared
options.B: Payment is released on the achievement of prescribed stages or milestones of the completed work, rather than against item-wise measurements of quantities
options.C: No payment is made till the whole project is handed over
options.D: Payment is made as a percentage of the schedule of rates for each item

e: In an EPC contract, payment is released on achievement of prescribed stages or milestones of completed work, rather than against item-wise measurements as in an item-rate contract.

q:
Consider the following statements regarding the price variation provisions of a works contract:
1. The adjustment is worked out with reference to the price indices of a base period defined in the contract, ordinarily linked to the period of the tender.
2. The rise or fall in the indices for the period of execution, compared with the base period, determines whether an amount becomes payable to the contractor or recoverable from him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: price variation is worked out against price indices of a base period defined in the contract, and rise or fall in indices for the execution period over the base decides payment or recovery.

q: A work providing a second running line alongside an existing single-line section, so that trains can be run in both directions without crossing delays on that section, is a work of:

options.A: Gauge conversion of the existing line
options.B: Restoration of a dismantled line
options.C: Construction of a new line on an entirely new alignment
options.D: Doubling of the existing line

e: A second running line alongside an existing single-line section, allowing trains both ways without crossing delays, is a work of doubling of the existing line.

q: In the percentage (departmental and general) charges levied on a work, the 'general charges' component, as distinct from the departmental charges, represents:

options.A: The cost of the tools and plant of the department used on the work
options.B: The cost of the establishment of the executive engineering department engaged on the work
options.C: The share of the cost of general administration of the Railway, such as accounts, audit and other general services attributable to the work
options.D: The dividend payable on the capital cost of the work

e: General charges represent the share of the Railway's general administration cost, such as accounts, audit and other general services, attributable to the work, distinct from departmental establishment and tools and plant charges.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Before procuring goods or services through the Government e-Marketplace, the buyer obtains a GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary (GARPTS) generated on the portal.
2. Where the required item is not available on GeM, the report so generated supports procurement through the normal procedure outside GeM.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: before procuring through GeM the buyer obtains a GeM Availability Report and Past Transaction Summary (GARPTS), and where the item is unavailable on GeM that report supports procurement outside GeM.

q: On the Government e-Marketplace, the CRAC generated by the buyer stands for:

options.A: Centralised Receipt and Allocation Certificate
options.B: Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate, generated after receipt and acceptance of the goods or services
options.C: Contractor's Registration and Accreditation Certificate
options.D: Certified Receipt for Advance Claims

e: CRAC on GeM stands for Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate, generated after receipt and acceptance of the goods or services by the consignee.

q: A 'custom bid' (BOQ-based bid) is resorted to on the Government e-Marketplace when:

options.A: The buyer wishes to avoid any competition among sellers
options.B: The value of the procurement is below the direct purchase limit
options.C: The seller demands payment in advance for the goods
options.D: The goods or services required by the buyer are not available under the standard categories or catalogue of the portal

e: A custom or BOQ-based bid on GeM is used when the required goods or services are not available under the portal's standard categories or catalogue.

q: In a buyer organisation registered on the Government e-Marketplace, the 'primary user' of the organisation:

options.A: Creates and administers the secondary users of the organisation, such as the indentor, consignee and the paying authority, and assigns their roles
options.B: Is the seller who supplies goods to the organisation
options.C: Is the officer who audits the GeM transactions of the organisation
options.D: Is the administrator of the GeM portal itself

e: The primary user of a buyer organisation on GeM creates and administers its secondary users, such as indentor, consignee and paying authority, and assigns their roles.

q: Before accepting his appointment, a person approached to act as an arbitrator in a dispute arising out of a works contract is required under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 to:

options.A: Deposit security for the due performance of his duties as arbitrator
options.B: Obtain the prior approval of the tender committee for his appointment
options.C: Disclose in writing any circumstances likely to give rise to justifiable doubts as to his independence or impartiality
options.D: Furnish a bank guarantee equal to the amount of the claim

e: Under Section 12 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, a person approached as arbitrator must disclose in writing circumstances likely to give rise to justifiable doubts as to his independence or impartiality.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. An arbitral tribunal is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 or the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 in conducting the proceedings before it.
2. An arbitral tribunal may decide a dispute ex aequo et bono (on the principles of equity and good conscience) only if the parties have expressly authorised it to do so.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: under Section 19 an arbitral tribunal is not bound by the CPC, 1908 or the Evidence Act, 1872, and under Section 28(2) it may decide ex aequo et bono only if expressly authorised by the parties.

q: Proceedings for the eviction of an unauthorised occupant of railway land and buildings, which are 'public premises', are conducted under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 by:

options.A: The tender committee of the division
options.B: The contractor who last worked on the premises
options.C: The District Magistrate of the district alone
options.D: The Estate Officer appointed for the purpose, who issues the show-cause notice and passes the eviction order

e: Eviction proceedings for unauthorised occupation of public premises are conducted under the Public Premises Act, 1971 by the Estate Officer, who issues the show-cause notice and passes the eviction order.

q: An order of eviction passed by the Estate Officer under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act, 1971 can be challenged in appeal before:

options.A: The arbitral tribunal constituted under the contract
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.D: The District Judge of the district in which the public premises are situated

e: An eviction order of the Estate Officer under the Public Premises Act, 1971 is appealable before the District Judge of the district in which the public premises are situated.

q: In the execution of a railway project, the shifting of existing utilities such as electric lines, water pipelines and cables which come in the way of the work is ordinarily arranged:

options.A: By the contractor at his own cost in every case, without any accountal
options.B: Through the agency owning the utility, as a deposit work, the cost of the shifting being charged to the estimate of the project
options.C: By the State Labour Department at its own cost
options.D: Only after the project has been completed and opened to traffic

e: Shifting of utilities in the way of a project is ordinarily arranged through the owning agency as a deposit work, the cost of shifting being charged to the project estimate.

q: For deciding the classification, manning and protection of a level crossing, the traffic density at the crossing is expressed in Train Vehicle Units (TVU), which are worked out as:

options.A: The number of trains passing the crossing in a week
options.B: The number of road vehicles using the crossing in a year
options.C: The product of the number of trains passing per day and the number of road vehicles passing per day
options.D: The ratio of road vehicles to trains passing the crossing

e: Train Vehicle Units are worked out as the product of the number of trains passing per day and the number of road vehicles passing per day at the level crossing.

q: A periodical census of traffic at level crossings is taken by the Railways principally in order to:

options.A: Review, on the basis of the traffic density (TVU) and other prescribed factors, the classification, manning and protection arrangements required at each crossing
options.B: Fix the licence fee payable by the road users of the crossing
options.C: Decide the rates to be quoted by contractors for works at the crossing
options.D: Work out the earnings of the stations adjoining the crossing

e: A periodical census of traffic at level crossings is taken to review, on traffic density (TVU) and other prescribed factors, the classification, manning and protection required at each crossing.

q: The licence fee charged for railway land licensed for commercial and allied purposes is fixed with reference to:

options.A: The book value of the land as recorded at the time of its acquisition
options.B: A percentage of the prevailing market value of the land, revised periodically in accordance with the extant instructions
options.C: The annual earnings of the nearest railway station
options.D: The security deposit furnished by the licensee

e: Licence fee for railway land licensed for commercial and allied purposes is fixed as a percentage of the prevailing market value of the land, revised periodically per extant instructions.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Enlistment of a contractor in a particular class entitles him to tender for works up to the monetary limit of that class.
2. Enlistment by itself guarantees that works will be allotted to the enlisted contractor.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: enlistment in a class entitles the contractor to tender up to that class's monetary limit, but enlistment by itself guarantees no allotment of works.

q: One of the canons of financial propriety laid down for expenditure from public funds is that:

options.A: Public money may be spent for the benefit of an individual officer at the discretion of the sanctioning authority
options.B: Every sanctioning authority should spend its allotment before the close of the financial year
options.C: Allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that, on the whole, they are not a source of profit to the recipient
options.D: Estimates should always be framed on the higher side so that savings do not arise

e: A canon of financial propriety under the GFR is that allowances granted to meet expenditure of a particular type should be so regulated that, on the whole, they are not a source of profit to the recipient.

q: A reverse auction conducted on the Government e-Marketplace for the procurement of goods or services differs from the e-auction used by the Railways for disposal of scrap in that:

options.A: The reverse auction is conducted only for the sale of scrap material
options.B: In a reverse auction the price is settled by the buyer in advance and sellers merely accept it
options.C: In a reverse auction the qualified sellers compete by successively lowering their prices, whereas an e-auction for scrap is a forward auction in which buyers bid the price upwards
options.D: A reverse auction can be held only after the contract has been awarded

e: In a GeM reverse auction qualified sellers bid downwards to win a buyer's requirement, while scrap e-auction is a forward auction where buyers bid upwards, as per GeM and Railway disposal procedures.

q: On the Government e-Marketplace, a reseller offering the products of an original equipment manufacturer (OEM) on the portal is required to be:

options.A: Authorised by the OEM to sell its products on the portal
options.B: A government department or a public sector undertaking
options.C: Registered as a works contractor with a zonal railway
options.D: Exempted from indicating the make and model of the products offered

e: A GeM reseller can offer an OEM product only if authorised by that OEM, as GeM seller registration requires OEM authorisation to ensure genuine products and accountability.

q: After the tenders for a work have been opened, a condition of the tender is relaxed in favour of one particular tenderer so as to improve his competitive position. Such a course is:

options.A: Permissible at the discretion of the tender committee
options.B: Permissible with the verbal approval of the accepting authority
options.C: Permissible if the tenderer is the lowest tenderer
options.D: Not permissible, as the conditions governing a tender cannot be altered after opening so as to favour one tenderer over others

e: Tender conditions cannot be altered after opening to favour one tenderer, as this violates equality and transparency in public procurement under the General Financial Rules and GCC for Works.

q: Where a member of a Tender Committee, such as the Finance member, does not agree with the recommendation proposed by the majority of the Committee, the correct course is that:

options.A: His disagreement is ignored and the minutes are issued as a unanimous recommendation
options.B: His views are recorded in the minutes of the Committee as a note of dissent, and the matter is decided by the accepting authority
options.C: The tender is automatically discharged in every such case
options.D: The Committee is dissolved and a fresh Committee is constituted

e: A dissenting Tender Committee member's note of dissent is recorded in the minutes and the accepting authority decides, as per Railway tender procedure; dissent does not automatically discharge the tender.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Expenditure incurred in excess of the grant voted by Parliament for a year is regularised by Parliament through an excess grant, after the Appropriation Accounts are examined by the Public Accounts Committee.
2. An excess over a grant can be regularised merely by an order of the General Manager of the Railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Excess over a voted grant needs Parliament's excess grant after PAC examination of Appropriation Accounts under Articles 114-115; a General Manager cannot regularise it.

q: Re-appropriation of funds in the railway budget from a work charged to Capital to a work charged to Revenue is:

options.A: Not permissible, funds provided under one such head not being transferable to meet expenditure under the other
options.B: Permissible at the discretion of the Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Permissible with the concurrence of the divisional Finance officer alone
options.D: Compulsory whenever savings arise under a capital work

e: Re-appropriation between Capital and Revenue is prohibited because voted funds under one demand/head cannot be diverted to another distinct head, as per Railway Budget and Financial Code rules.

q: In the abstract of cost forming part of the detailed estimate of a work, the provisions towards work-charged establishment and towards departmental and general (percentage) charges are:

options.A: Included in the rates quoted by the tenderers for the items of work
options.B: Shown separately, in addition to the cost of the work proper worked out from the quantities and rates
options.C: Borne by the contractor and therefore not shown in the estimate at all
options.D: Charged to the revenue working expenses of the division directly

e: In a detailed estimate, work-charged establishment and departmental charges are shown separately in the abstract of cost over and above quantities multiplied by rates, as per Engineering Code.

q: An incentive (bonus) clause sometimes provided in the special conditions of a major works contract operates so that:

options.A: Liquidated damages can never be levied under the contract
options.B: The contractor's rates are enhanced for the whole work after its completion
options.C: The security deposit of the contractor is refunded before completion of the work
options.D: The contractor is paid an additional amount for completing the work ahead of the stipulated date of completion, as provided in the contract

e: An incentive clause in GCC special conditions pays a bonus for completion before the stipulated date; it is a contractual reward for early completion, distinct from liquidated damages for delay.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the price variation clause of a works contract, the material component of the adjustment is worked out with reference to the Wholesale Price Index.
2. The labour component of the adjustment is worked out with reference to the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct. Under the GCC price variation clause, material adjustment uses the Wholesale Price Index and labour adjustment uses the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers.

q: The individual petty works and repairs executed under a zonal contract are subject to:

options.A: A prescribed ceiling on the value of each individual work order issued under the contract
options.B: A separate open tender for every petty work, in addition to the zonal contract
options.C: The sanction of the Railway Board for every work order
options.D: No monetary limit of any kind on any single work order

e: A zonal contract covers petty works through work orders, each subject to a prescribed ceiling value, as per Engineering Code and GCC zonal contract conditions to prevent splitting or misuse.

q: Along with his tender for a work on IREPS, a tenderer is ordinarily required to furnish a self-declaration to the effect that:

options.A: He has never executed any work for any other employer
options.B: He has not been banned or debarred from business dealings, and no contract of his has been terminated on account of his default, during the period specified in the tender documents
options.C: He will engage only departmental labour for executing the work
options.D: His rates are not open to any negotiation in any circumstance

e: IREPS tenderers must self-declare that they are not banned or debarred and no contract was terminated for their default in the specified period, as required by tender eligibility conditions.

q: Administrative approval has been accorded to a proposed work, but the detailed estimate of the work has not yet been technically sanctioned. In this position:

options.A: The work can be commenced on the strength of the administrative approval alone
options.B: Tenders for the work can be finalised and the work awarded forthwith
options.C: The contractor can be allowed to start the work in anticipation of the sanction
options.D: The work cannot be commenced until the detailed estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority and funds are allotted for it

e: Administrative approval alone does not permit commencement. Work needs technical sanction of the detailed estimate and allotment of funds, as per Engineering Code provisions on sanction to expenditure.

q: Where trees standing on land required for a railway project have to be felled, the position is that:

options.A: The trees may be felled by the contractor without any permission and without any charge to the project
options.B: The permission of the competent forest authority is obtained as applicable, and the cost of felling and of compensatory plantation, where leviable, is charged to the project
options.C: The cost is recovered from the workmen engaged on the project
options.D: The trees are transferred to the adjoining station as its property

e: Felling trees on project land needs permission of the competent forest authority where applicable, and felling plus compensatory plantation cost, if leviable, is charged to the project estimate.

q: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM), the national public procurement portal for goods and services, is operated by:

options.A: A special purpose vehicle in the form of a not-for-profit company set up under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry
options.B: The Railway Board for all government departments
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: A consortium of public sector banks

e: GeM is operated by GeM SPV, a not-for-profit company under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, set up as the national public procurement portal for goods and services.

q: Under the public procurement policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, government buyers, including the Railways, are required to:

options.A: Procure exclusively from micro and small enterprises in all cases
options.B: Award all works contracts to micro and small enterprises on nomination
options.C: Exempt micro and small enterprises from furnishing any performance security in all cases
options.D: Procure a prescribed minimum share of their annual procurement of goods and services from micro and small enterprises, with sub-targets for enterprises owned by Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes and by women

e: The MSME Public Procurement Policy, 2012 requires a prescribed minimum annual procurement from Micro and Small Enterprises, with sub-targets for SC/ST-owned and women-owned enterprises.

q: An application for setting aside an arbitral award under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is required to be made:

options.A: At any time, there being no period of limitation for such an application
options.B: Within five years of the date of the arbitral award
options.C: Within three months of the date on which the party making the application received the arbitral award
options.D: Only before the award is signed by the arbitral tribunal

e: Under Section 34(3) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an application to set aside an award must be made within three months of receipt of the award by the applicant.

q: In making an arbitral award in a works dispute, the arbitral tribunal may award interest:

options.A: Only for the period after the date of the award
options.B: Only if the contractor has furnished a bank guarantee for the claim amount
options.C: For the periods before the reference, during the pendency of the proceedings and after the award, as provided in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 and subject to the contract
options.D: At a rate fixed by the tender committee of the Railway

e: Section 31(7) of the Arbitration Act permits the tribunal to award interest for pre-reference, pendente lite and post-award periods, unless the contract otherwise provides.

q: After an arbitral award has been made, the correction of a computational, clerical or typographical error appearing in the award is dealt with under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by:

options.A: Filing a fresh arbitration reference for the whole dispute
options.B: The arbitral tribunal itself, on the request of a party or on its own initiative, within the scope of the correction provisions of the Act
options.C: The tender committee which accepted the original tender
options.D: The Accounts office, by a corrigendum to the final bill

e: Under Section 33 of the Arbitration Act, the tribunal itself corrects computational, clerical or typographical errors on a party's request or on its own initiative, without a fresh reference.

q: The 'fast track procedure' provided in the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 is a procedure under which:

options.A: The dispute is decided by the Engineer without any arbitral tribunal
options.B: The award is made without any pleadings by the parties
options.C: The contractor is debarred from presenting any claim
options.D: The dispute is decided by a sole arbitrator, ordinarily on the basis of the written pleadings and documents of the parties, within an expedited time frame

e: Section 29B fast track procedure provides decision by a sole arbitrator mainly on written pleadings and documents within an expedited time frame, with oral hearing only if needed.

q: In a public-private partnership concession for a railway project, an escrow account is provided for principally in order that:

options.A: All the receipts and payments of the project are routed through the account and applied in the order of priority agreed with the lenders and the authority
options.B: The concessionaire can keep his personal funds separate from his other business
options.C: The earnest money of all the bidders is retained permanently
options.D: The salary of the staff of the special purpose vehicle is paid in cash

e: In a PPP concession, the escrow account routes all project receipts and payments and applies them in the agreed priority waterfall for lenders and the authority, as per the concession agreement.

q: Where a concession agreement for a public-private partnership project is terminated before the end of the concession period, the compensation, if any, payable to the concessionaire is governed by:

options.A: The discretion of the contractor executing the balance work
options.B: The termination payment provisions contained in the concession agreement itself, which ordinarily vary according to whether the termination is due to the default of the concessionaire or of the authority
options.C: The rates quoted in the original tender for the project
options.D: The liquidated damages clause of the General Conditions of Contract for Works

e: On early termination of a PPP concession, compensation is governed by the termination payment clauses of the concession agreement itself, which differ for concessionaire default and authority default.

q: Selection of a consultant from a single source, without competition, may be justified under the procurement rules where:

options.A: The assignment is a natural continuation of an earlier assignment of the same consultant and continuity of the same technical approach is essential
options.B: The executing agency wishes to save the time taken by a competitive selection, as a matter of routine
options.C: The consultant offers to work at a nominal fee without any agreement
options.D: More than one qualified consultant is available in the market for the assignment

e: Single-source selection of a consultant is justified under GFR Rule 178-type grounds where continuity is essential, such as a natural continuation of an earlier assignment with the same technical approach.

q: Pre-qualification and eligibility criteria prescribed in the tender documents for a work should be:

options.A: Kept so stringent that only one known firm can qualify for the work
options.B: Altered after the issue of the tender notice to suit a particular tenderer
options.C: Decided by the tenderers themselves at the pre-bid conference
options.D: Proportionate to the nature and value of the work, so that competition is not restricted by criteria unrelated to the capacity needed for the work

e: Pre-qualification criteria must be proportionate to the nature and value of the work under GFR principles of fairness and competition; unrelated stringent criteria improperly restrict competition.

q: Vacant railway land entrusted for commercial development is ordinarily leased out by the Rail Land Development Authority through:

options.A: Free transfer to the State Government
options.B: Nomination of the first applicant for the land
options.C: Allotment at the book value of the land recorded in the asset register
options.D: A competitive bidding process, such as e-auction, so that the market value of the land parcel is realised

e: RLDA leases vacant railway land for commercial development through competitive bidding such as e-auction, so that market value is realised transparently, as per Railway Land Policy and RLDA procedure.

q: Where a works contractor is permitted under the contract to occupy railway land or buildings at the site for his site office, stores and labour camps, he is liable to pay for such occupation:

options.A: Nothing, such occupation being free in all cases
options.B: Licence fee and other charges at the rates provided in the contract, recoverable from the amounts payable to him
options.C: A share of the earnings of the serving station
options.D: The departmental charges of the whole work a second time

e: A contractor occupying railway land or buildings for site office, stores or camps pays licence fee and charges at contract rates, recoverable from his bills, as per GCC for Works conditions.

q: Where a works tender is submitted by a joint venture of firms, the earnest money and the performance guarantee for the work are ordinarily furnished:

options.A: Separately by every member of the joint venture for the full amount
options.B: By the Railway itself on behalf of the joint venture
options.C: By the lead member of the joint venture on behalf of the joint venture, in accordance with the tender conditions
options.D: Only after the completion of the work by the joint venture

e: In a joint venture tender, earnest money and performance guarantee are ordinarily furnished by the lead member on behalf of the joint venture, as provided in the GCC and tender conditions for JV.

q: In addition to cash, bank guarantees and fixed deposit receipts, the modes in which earnest money and performance security for government contracts may now be furnished include:

options.A: A personal surety bond of another contractor
options.B: Post-dated cheques of the tenderer
options.C: A promissory note executed by the tenderer's proprietor
options.D: Insurance surety bonds and electronic bank guarantees (e-BG), as permitted by the extant government instructions

e: Government instructions now permit earnest money and performance security through insurance surety bonds and electronic bank guarantees (e-BG) in addition to cash, bank guarantee and FDR.

q: Where a seller registered on the Government e-Marketplace repeatedly fails to supply the goods ordered or otherwise defaults on the portal, the action that may be taken against him on the portal includes:

options.A: Raising of an incident against the seller and, in accordance with the portal's incident management policy, suspension or debarment of the seller from the portal
options.B: Levy of liquidated damages under the General Conditions of Contract for Works
options.C: Termination of the seller's registration as a works contractor of the Railway
options.D: Recovery of the amount from the earnest money of other sellers

e: Repeated GeM defaults attract an incident on the portal and, under the GeM Incident Management Policy, suspension or debarment of the seller from GeM, distinct from Railway works GCC action.

q: After the consignee on the Government e-Marketplace has generated the Consignee's Receipt and Acceptance Certificate (CRAC) for goods received, the payment to the seller is required to be released by the buyer:

options.A: Only at the close of the financial year
options.B: Within the period prescribed in the GeM terms, ordinarily ten days of the generation of the CRAC
options.C: After the goods have been fully consumed by the consignee
options.D: Only after a fresh tender is invited for the same goods

e: After generation of CRAC on GeM, the buyer must release payment within the prescribed period, ordinarily ten days, as per GeM terms and conditions and GFR payment timelines.

q: The validity period of the tenders for a work expired without any extension being sought from the tenderers, and no acceptance was communicated to the lowest tenderer within that period. The earnest money of that tenderer is:

options.A: Liable to be forfeited for failure to accept the work
options.B: Adjusted towards the security deposit of the work automatically
options.C: Not liable to be forfeited, the tenderer being no longer bound by his offer after the expiry of its validity, and is refundable to him
options.D: Retained by the Railways until another tender for the work is finalised

e: If tender validity expires without acceptance, the tenderer is no longer bound by his offer, so earnest money cannot be forfeited and must be refunded, as per GCC tender conditions.

q: A party to a works contract objects that the arbitration agreement itself is not valid and that the arbitral tribunal therefore has no authority to decide the dispute. Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, such an objection is dealt with on the principle that:

options.A: Only a civil court can ever decide the question, the tribunal having no power in the matter
options.B: The arbitral tribunal is competent to rule on its own jurisdiction, including an objection to the existence or validity of the arbitration agreement
options.C: The objection automatically terminates the arbitral proceedings
options.D: The objection can be raised only after the award has been made

e: Under Section 16, competence-competence, of the Arbitration Act, the tribunal itself can rule on its own jurisdiction, including objections to existence or validity of the arbitration agreement.

q: Even before arbitral proceedings in a works dispute have commenced, a party which needs urgent protection, such as securing the amount in dispute or preserving property connected with the contract, may, under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996:

options.A: Apply to the court for interim measures of protection
options.B: Forfeit the security deposit of the other party on its own authority
options.C: Stop all payments due under every contract of the other party
options.D: Direct the tender committee to decide the dispute summarily

e: Section 9 of the Arbitration Act allows a party, before or during arbitral proceedings, to apply to the court for interim measures such as securing the amount or preserving property.

q: A supplier who has sold materials to a works contractor, but has no contract of his own with the Railways, sues the Railways directly on the works contract for the price of those materials. Under the doctrine of privity of contract:

options.A: The supplier can enforce the works contract because his materials were used in the work
options.B: The Railways must pay the supplier and recover the amount from the contractor
options.C: Only the parties to a contract can enforce it or be held liable under it, so a stranger to the works contract cannot sue upon it
options.D: The supplier becomes a party to the works contract once his materials reach the site

e: Under privity of contract, only parties to a contract can enforce it or be liable under it; a supplier to the contractor, being a stranger to the Railway works contract, cannot sue Railways on it.

q: For a procurement made through the Government e-Marketplace in which performance security is required from the seller, the security is furnished on the portal in the form of:

options.A: A cash deposit made at the nearest railway cash office
options.B: A personal bond executed by the proprietor of the selling firm
options.C: A post-dated cheque in favour of the buyer organisation
options.D: An electronic performance bank guarantee (ePBG) furnished through the portal

e: Where performance security is required on GeM, the seller furnishes it as an electronic performance bank guarantee (ePBG) through the portal, as per GeM conditions.

q: In a buyer organisation working on the Government e-Marketplace, the role of the Paying Authority (the DDO/PAO user) in respect of an order placed on the portal is to:

options.A: Create the bids and place the orders on behalf of the organisation
options.B: Release the payment to the seller after the consignee has accepted the goods or services and generated the receipt and acceptance certificate
options.C: Inspect the goods at the consignee's premises and reject defective lots
options.D: Register and authorise the sellers offering goods on the portal

e: On GeM, the Paying Authority (DDO/PAO) releases payment to the seller after the consignee accepts the goods or services and generates CRAC; ordering and inspection are other users' roles.

q: Goods supplied against an order on the Government e-Marketplace are inspected by the consignee and are found not to conform to the specifications of the order. The correct course for the consignee is to:

options.A: Refuse acceptance of the non-conforming goods, not generate the acceptance certificate for them and raise the matter on the portal for replacement or other action against the seller
options.B: Accept the goods and adjust the difference by a cut in the seller's next bill
options.C: Generate the acceptance certificate and return the goods at the buyer's own cost
options.D: Pay for the goods in full and write off the loss as a departmental charge

e: Non-conforming GeM supplies must not be accepted or certified in CRAC; the consignee refuses them and raises the matter on the portal for replacement or action, as per GeM procedure.

q: Powers delegated to an authority under the Schedule of Powers are proposed to be passed on by that authority to an officer subordinate to it. The correct position is that:

options.A: Delegated powers can always be sub-delegated freely at the discretion of the delegate
options.B: Sub-delegation converts the subordinate into the accepting authority for all tenders
options.C: Further delegation (re-delegation) is permissible only where the Schedule of Powers or the delegation itself expressly provides for it
options.D: Sub-delegation requires the prior approval of the contractor executing the work

e: Powers under the Schedule of Powers can be re-delegated only where the Schedule or the delegation expressly permits it; delegated power has no implied power of further delegation.

q: The performance of an enlisted works contractor is repeatedly found unsatisfactory in the works executed by him, though no single default justifies banning of business dealings. At the periodical review of enlistment, the action that can be taken against him includes:

options.A: Levy of liquidated damages on works he has not yet been awarded
options.B: Recovery of the loss from the earnest money of other enlisted contractors
options.C: Forfeiture of earnest money deposited by him for tenders not yet opened
options.D: Downgrading him to a lower class of enlistment, or removal of his name from the approved list, after following the prescribed procedure

e: At periodical review of contractor enlistment, unsatisfactory performance can lead to downgrading to a lower class or removal from the approved list after prescribed procedure, as per contractor registration rules.

q: In a steel girder bridge executed under a works contract, the bearings provided under the girders are arranged so that:

options.A: Both ends of every girder are rigidly fixed to the substructure
options.B: One end is fixed while the other end is provided with expansion bearings, so that the girder can expand and contract with changes of temperature
options.C: The girders rest directly on the masonry without any bearings at all
options.D: Bearings are provided only under bridges carrying road traffic

e: Steel girder bearings provide one fixed end and one expansion end, allowing thermal expansion and contraction of the girder, as per Bridge Code practice; fixing both ends would induce harmful stresses.

q: 'Soling' provided in the foundation of a structure or under a pavement in a works contract consists of:

options.A: A layer of stones, boulders or bricks laid on the prepared ground to provide a firm base for the foundation or pavement above it
options.B: A coat of bitumen painted over the finished surface of a road
options.C: A layer of lean concrete used for levelling the top of a wall
options.D: The filling placed behind the abutment of a bridge

e: Soling is a layer of stones, boulders or bricks laid on prepared ground to give a firm base for a foundation or pavement, as defined in standard works specifications and schedule items.

q: In a buyer organisation on the Government e-Marketplace, the user designated as the 'Buyer', as distinct from the primary user, the consignee and the paying authority, is the one who:

options.A: Audits the procurement transactions of the organisation
options.B: Sells goods to the organisation through the portal
options.C: Prepares and publishes the bids on the portal and places the orders on the basis of the indents and approvals of the organisation
options.D: Receives and inspects the goods at the delivery point

e: On GeM, the Buyer user prepares and publishes bids and places orders based on indents and approvals, distinct from the primary user, consignee who receives goods, and paying authority.

q: A division engages a facility-management service for its office buildings through the Government e-Marketplace. Payment to the service provider for a completed period of service is released on the portal:

options.A: In advance for the whole contract period at the time of placing the order
options.B: Only after the expiry of the contract, in a single instalment
options.C: On the basis of the seller's invoice alone, without any acceptance by the buyer
options.D: After the consignee certifies the satisfactory rendering of the service for that period and generates the acceptance for it on the portal

e: For GeM services, payment for a period is released only after the consignee certifies satisfactory rendering of service for that period and generates acceptance on the portal.

q: During the pendency of arbitral proceedings in a works dispute, interim protection of the subject-matter of the dispute, where the arbitration agreement does not exclude it, can be ordered under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 by:

options.A: The tender committee which accepted the original tender
options.B: The arbitral tribunal itself, on the application of a party
options.C: The Engineer-in-charge of the work alone
options.D: The Accounts office dealing with the contract

e: Under Section 17 of the Arbitration Act, the arbitral tribunal itself can order interim measures during proceedings, unless the arbitration agreement excludes that power.

q: A works contractor houses the labour engaged by him in a camp at the site of the work. The provision of drinking water, sanitary facilities and first-aid arrangements for the labour at the camp is, in the first instance, the responsibility of:

options.A: The contractor who has engaged the labour
options.B: The Railway's medical department
options.C: The State Labour Department
options.D: The workmen themselves, acting collectively

e: Under GCC and labour welfare conditions, the contractor who engages labour is primarily responsible for drinking water, sanitation and first-aid for his labour camp at site.

q: For a complete track renewal work, rails and sleepers are supplied by the Railways free of cost to the contractor, who has only to lay them. A quantity of the rails so issued is found short with the contractor at the completion of the work. In this position:

options.A: The shortage is ignored, the materials having been supplied free
options.B: The cost of the shortage is shared equally between the Railways and the contractor
options.C: The contractor remains accountable for the free-issue materials entrusted to him, and the cost of the materials not accounted for is recoverable from him
options.D: The shortage is adjusted against the earnest money of the unsuccessful tenderers

e: Free-issue Railway materials remain Railway property in the contractor's custody; he is accountable for them and cost of unaccounted shortage is recoverable, as per GCC material accounting conditions.

q: While a work is in progress, the executive finds that the provision made for contingencies in the sanctioned estimate is exhausted and proposes to meet the departmental and general charges of the work out of that provision. This proposal is objectionable because:

options.A: Contingencies and departmental charges are one and the same provision
options.B: Departmental charges of a work are borne by the contractor and never appear in its estimate
options.C: Contingencies can be used for any purpose at the discretion of the executive
options.D: Departmental and general charges are provided separately in the abstract of cost of the estimate, over and above the cost of the work proper, and cannot be met by diverting the contingencies provision

e: Contingencies and departmental charges are separate provisions in the estimate abstract. Contingencies cover unforeseen petty items and cannot be diverted to meet separately provided departmental charges.

q: A building work has been completed, taken over and its accounts closed after the defect liability period. A repair that becomes necessary thereafter, owing to ordinary wear in use, is to be carried out:

options.A: By reopening the closed work and booking the cost to its original estimate
options.B: As ordinary repairs and maintenance by the department which owns and uses the building, chargeable to Revenue
options.C: By the original contractor at his own cost, the liability being perpetual
options.D: By recovering the cost from the security deposit retained for the work

e: After a work is completed, taken over and closed, ordinary wear repairs are revenue maintenance by the owning department, not a charge to the closed capital work, as per Engineering Code.

q: After the Letter of Acceptance is issued, the successful tenderer neither executes the formal agreement nor commences the work within the period stipulated. The course open to the Railways under the contract conditions is to:

options.A: Cancel the acceptance, forfeit the earnest money/security available, and arrange the work through another agency at the risk and cost of the defaulting tenderer
options.B: Wait indefinitely, the tenderer being free to start the work at any time
options.C: Extend the period for signing the agreement as a matter of course, without any consequence
options.D: Pay him compensation for the mobilisation he claims to have made

e: If the successful tenderer fails to sign the agreement or start work after LOA, Railways may cancel acceptance, forfeit earnest money/security and execute at his risk and cost, as per GCC.

q: A contractor completes a work well before the stipulated date and claims a bonus for early completion, but the contract contains no incentive or bonus clause. His claim is:

options.A: Payable at the rate applicable to liquidated damages, in reverse
options.B: Payable from the savings in the sanctioned estimate of the work
options.C: Not maintainable, a bonus for early completion being payable only where the contract expressly provides for it
options.D: Payable with the approval of the Engineer-in-charge of the work

e: A bonus for early completion is payable only if the contract expressly contains an incentive/bonus clause; without such a clause no bonus arises by analogy to liquidated damages.

q: The completion of a work is delayed solely by the contractor's slow progress and extension of time is granted for the extended period, during which the price indices rise sharply. Under the price variation provisions of the contract, the adjustment for the extended period is ordinarily worked out:

options.A: With the indices of the extended period, so that the contractor gets the full benefit of the rise
options.B: At twice the normal rate, as a penalty on the Railways
options.C: By the tender committee on an ad hoc basis for each bill
options.D: With the indices frozen at those prevailing on the original stipulated date of completion, as provided in the contract

e: Where delay is due to the contractor, price variation for the extended period is worked out with indices frozen at the original stipulated completion date, as per the GCC price variation clause.
